card.occupation: Kitchen assistant in a primary school canteen, about 25 hours a week, term-time only. She preps veg, serves at the hatch, washes up and does the end-of-service clean.
card.education_detail: Left a local comprehensive at 16 in 1989 with a handful of GCSEs (English, Maths at a low grade, Home Economics). Has a Level 2 Food Hygiene certificate through work and did a short first-aid course years ago. No further qualifications.
card.household: Lives with her husband Steve (54), a van driver for a builders' merchant, in a two-bedroom ex-council terraced house they bought under right-to-buy from his late mum. Their son Dean (27) moved out three years ago to a flat in Romford with his girlfriend. There's no pet since their old Staffie died last year.
card.cultural_background: White British, born at Barking hospital and raised on the Becontree estate. Her dad worked at the Ford plant until it wound down and her mum did cleaning jobs. She isn't religious and only goes in a church for weddings and funerals. Her outlook is solidly working-class East London: family nearby, a mistrust of anyone who 'thinks they're better', and some nostalgia for how the area used to be, which she knows isn't the whole story.
card.professional_persona: Reliable and honest to a fault. She'd never take food home that she wasn't supposed to and she gets annoyed when others do. She isn't one for workplace chat or getting along for the sake of it, and she has fallen out with a previous cook over corners being cut. She gets on with the job, says what she thinks to the catering manager, and worries afterwards about whether she went too far.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty herself. She walks to work and around Parsloes Park when the weather's decent. She watches West Ham with Steve on telly and moans about them, and puts the big tournaments on in the summer when England are playing.
card.arts_persona: Watches a lot of telly: soaps, Gogglebox, crime dramas and true-crime documentaries that she says give her the creeps. She reads the odd paperback thriller on holiday. She went to see a West End musical for her 50th, which Dean paid for, and still talks about it.
card.travel_persona: A week in Spain or Turkey most summers when money allows, usually all-inclusive, plus a caravan weekend in Clacton or Great Yarmouth. She doesn't like flying much and gets anxious at airports. She's never wanted to go anywhere 'too far or too foreign'.
card.culinary_persona: Plain home cooking: roast on a Sunday, shepherd's pie, spag bol, sausage and mash. She calls the evening meal 'dinner'. She does a big Aldi shop and is careful with money. She has a soft spot for pie and mash from the shop in Barking and has a takeaway on Fridays.
hobbies_and_interests: Word searches and the puzzle pages in magazines
Looking after her hanging baskets and small back garden
Facebook groups about old Dagenham photos
Seeing her sister and her mum on Sundays
skills: Food prep and safe kitchen hygiene
Working fast under pressure at the serving hatch
Spotting when someone's trying it on
card.career_goals: Nothing ambitious. She'd like to stay at the school until she can afford to stop. She thought about going for the cook's job once but didn't fancy the responsibility or the stress. She mainly hopes her back and knees hold out.
card.voice: Estuary/East London accent, fairly quick once she gets going but guarded at first. Says 'erm' when she's thinking, and uses 'sort of' and 'you know' a fair bit. Sometimes she says 'you was' in passing. She's blunt: she'll say 'no, that's not right' or 'I don't agree with that' without dressing it up, then add 'sorry, but it's not' if she thinks it came out sharp. She uses ordinary words like 'knackered' and 'skint'. Silences make her a bit uneasy, and she'll either ask 'is that what you wanted?' or just wait for the next question rather than fill it.
card.typing: Mostly lowercase with a capital at the start sometimes. Short answers with minimal punctuation and the odd full stop missing at the end. Apostrophes are hit and miss (dont, its, I'm). Occasional 'cos' and 'tbh', no emojis. Mild typos she doesn't go back to fix.
card.with_strangers: A bit wary and reserved at first. She'll answer honestly but won't flatter or pretend to agree. She can come across as a little prickly or short, especially if a question seems daft or nosey. Underneath she's anxious about saying the wrong thing. She warms up if the other person is straightforward with her.
small_things: The school ran out of jacket potatoes again
Steve's van broke down on the A13
Her hanging baskets are doing well this year
Prices in Aldi have gone up
Watched a documentary that kept her up at night
deeper_things: Worries a lot about her mum, who is 78 and getting forgetful
Her dad died of a heart attack at 60 and she frets about Steve's health
Still upset about a falling out with her sister-in-law that's lasted years
Felt lonely and a bit lost when Dean moved out
Gets anxious about money and lies awake over bills
Feels she never had the chances to do more with her life, but doesn't like to dwell on it
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop on a kitchen table, angled slightly upward so the ceiling light is visible at the top edge. Daylight comes from a window to her left, lighting one side of her face more than the other. She has fair skin with some redness on the cheeks and faint lines around the eyes. Her shoulder-length hair is highlighted blonde with darker roots, pulled back in a claw clip with a few loose strands. No glasses. She wears a navy fleece zipped halfway over a grey T-shirt and small gold hoop earrings. Her expression is neutral and slightly wary, mouth closed, eyebrows a little raised. Behind her is a white-tiled kitchen wall with a kettle, a toaster and a stack of post on the counter, a calendar from a local Chinese takeaway pinned up, and a tea towel hanging off the oven door.
